source_name: e-Prokurimi — Kosovo national e-procurement portal (KRPP/PPRC)
why_relevant: Legally mandatory central publication point for every contracting authority in Kosovo under Law No. 04/L-042. All contract notices (njoftim per kontrate), award notices (njoftim per dhenie te kontrates, form B08) and signature notices for banking, card, ATM, POS, core-banking and cash-handling lots are published here first, by the buyer itself. Highest-density primary source for workstream A2 in this country.

source_name: e-Prokurimi notice detail endpoint (DokumentPodaciFrm.aspx?id=)
why_relevant: Individual notice records (including B08 contract award notices) are exposed at a stable id-addressable URL and are search-engine indexed, i.e. individual banking/payments award notices can be fetched directly once an id or notice number is known from the OCDS API.

source_name: KRPP OCDS Web API (krppAPI) — open contracting data for Kosovo
why_relevant: Machine-readable OCDS feed of the national platform. Documented endpoints include TenderRelease, Tender, TenderUpdate, Award, Bid, Tenderers, Parties, PartyRole and Document, with filters for date range, party name, tender name, tender number and value threshold — exactly the shape needed to pull banking/payments award notices and winning suppliers on a schedule. This is the single best long-term collection channel for the cell.

source_name: OCP Data Registry — Kosovo: Public Procurement Regulatory Commission (bulk OCDS downloads)
why_relevant: Mirrors and documents the KRPP OCDS publication: coverage March 2016 – March 2026, monthly refresh, ~75,710 tenders / 211,313 parties, downloadable as JSONL.gz, XLSX and CSV per year or all-time. Gives an instant historical backfill of Kosovo award notices without hammering the national portal, plus a documented data-quality assessment.

source_name: KRPP — Komisioni Rregullativ i Prokurimit Publik (institutional site)
why_relevant: The regulator that owns the platform. Publishes rules, standard forms (including the B08 award-notice form), opinions, blacklists and links out to AQP and OSHP — the actor map for the whole cell starts here.

source_name: KRPP annual reports on public procurement activities (Raporti Vjetor)
why_relevant: Statutory annual statistical report on all public contracts signed 1 Jan – 31 Dec, by authority, procedure type and value. Provides the denominator and market-structure context for banking/payments lots, and flags year-on-year shifts in centralised vs decentralised buying.

source_name: e-Prokurimi secondary legislation — Rules and Operational Guideline for Public Procurement (sq / sr / en)
why_relevant: Authoritative trilingual glossary generator: the same rulebook exists in Albanian, Serbian and English, so notice-type names, form codes and field labels can be aligned across languages (e.g. 'Njoftim për dhënie të kontratës' = 'Obaveštenje o dodeli ugovora' = 'Contract award notice'). Also defines publication obligations and thresholds that determine what will and will not appear on the platform.

source_name: AQP — Agjencia Qendrore e Prokurimit (Central Procurement Agency)
why_relevant: Runs centralised procurement on behalf of all Kosovo public institutions (reported >EUR 40m/yr in centralised contracts). Cross-government banking, payment-processing and cash-handling services are exactly the 'commonly used item' category that gets centralised here, so a single AQP framework contract can replace dozens of individual authority tenders — a structural blind spot if only the notice feed is monitored.

source_name: OSHP — Organi Shqyrtues i Prokurimit (Procurement Review Body)
why_relevant: Independent complaints body whose binding decisions can annul or re-run banking/payments awards. Decisions reveal bidder identities, evaluation criteria and pricing disputes that the award notice itself does not disclose, and they are the earliest signal that a contract will not proceed as announced. Also publishes an economic-operator blacklist.

source_name: Databaza e vendimeve të OSHP (oshp.dplus.org) — civil-society mirror of review-body decisions
why_relevant: Third-party searchable database of OSHP decisions, typically easier to query and to scrape than the official site, and useful as a cross-check when the official listing is incomplete or reorganised.

source_name: Prokurimi Hapur / Open Procurement Transparency Portal
why_relevant: Automatically ingests PPRC/KRPP data and normalises public contracts awarded since 2010 (~48k contracts extracted) into a browsable buyer/supplier/value view. Faster than the raw API for supplier-side questions ('which vendors win payment-infrastructure lots') and useful for validating our own OCDS parsing.

source_name: Flamujt e Kuq / Red Flags Kosovo
why_relevant: Risk-scoring layer built on the same PPRC data, flagging single-bid, short-deadline and repeat-winner patterns. For banking/payments lots this is a cheap way to spot captured or non-competitive segments without doing our own statistics.

source_name: BQK — Central Bank of the Republic of Kosovo, Tenders page
why_relevant: The single most domain-relevant contracting authority in the cell: the central bank buys payment-system, cash-handling, currency-processing and core IT services. BQK publishes its own contract and award notices (B08-style PDFs) on its site under its own December 2024 procurement rule, which means some BQK procurement may be visible here in a form or timing that differs from the central platform.

source_name: Contracting-authority mirror pages (e.g. Dogana e Kosovës notice files, Ministry of Health OSHP decision files)
why_relevant: Individual Kosovo authorities mirror their own B08 award notices as PDFs in predictable shared folders. These mirrors are often reachable and indexable when the central portal's document application is behind login, giving a fallback retrieval route for specific notices (customs, tax administration, ministries — all buyers of payment and cash-handling services).

source_name: Municipal e-Prokurimi notice republication pages (example: Komuna e Vushtrrisë)
why_relevant: Municipalities are numerous contracting authorities that buy POS/card-acceptance and municipal-fee collection services, and many republish their e-Prokurimi notices on their own sites. Useful for local-level coverage and as a low-friction crawl target across ~38 municipal domains.

source_name: ZKA — Zyra Kombëtare e Auditimit (National Audit Office of Kosovo)
why_relevant: Audits procurement practice including dedicated performance audits of centralised procurement ('Vlera për para në prokurimet e centralizuara'). Audit reports name contracts, values and failures that award notices present neutrally, and often reveal contracts that were signed but never properly noticed.

source_name: KALLXO.com (BIRN Kosovo) — procurement investigative tags
why_relevant: Sustained investigative coverage of Kosovo procurement, including OSHP annulments and blacklistings, with tag pages per institution (AQP, KRPP, OSHP). Gives narrative context and early warning on contested banking/IT lots; frequently surfaces documents not otherwise online.

source_name: CEFTA Transparency Pack — Public Procurement (Kosovo)
why_relevant: Regional trade-portal page describing Kosovo's procurement regime and access points in English; useful for regime comparison across the Western Balkans and for confirming the official entry points from a neutral multilateral source.

source_name: Transparent Public Procurement Rating — Kosovo country page
why_relevant: Independent methodological assessment of how complete and accessible Kosovo's procurement publication actually is. Directly informs how much we should trust the notice feed as a complete census of banking/payments lots.

source_name: Open Contracting Partnership — Kosovo transparency case study
why_relevant: Explains how the Kosovo OCDS publication was built, who the civil-society consumers are, and what the known data gaps are. This is the fastest snowball hub from the platform to the whole downstream ecosystem (prokurimihapur, redflags, Democracy Plus, Open Data Kosovo).

source_name: Commercial tender aggregators covering Kosovo (TendersInfo, BidDetail, GlobalTenders, TendersOnTime)
why_relevant: Paywalled English-language resellers of Kosovo notices. Their free teaser listings are occasionally useful for keyword discovery (e.g. surfacing that an ATM or core-banking lot exists), but they are intermediaries with unknown latency and coverage — never a substitute for the platform.

source_name: IOM Kosovo procurement & tenders (international-organisation buyer in-country)
why_relevant: International organisations operating in Kosovo procure payment/cash-transfer and card-issuance services but are NOT subject to the national Public Procurement Law, so their notices never appear on e-Prokurimi. Covering them closes a real hole in the A2 census.

source_name: BQK procurement rulebook (Rregulla/Pravila për prokurim në BQK)
why_relevant: BQK appears to operate under its OWN Executive-Board-adopted procurement rules (amended Oct 2024) rather than purely the general Public Procurement Law. This determines whether BQK payment-system tenders ever appear on e-Prokurimi/OSHP at all — a critical scoping fact for any tender-tracking pipeline.
